citations.claim: body 1 x is NaN at first violating step

counterfactual.change: Set controller.enabled from true to false (single field). This removes controller forces/work, leaving gravity+collisions only; scenario then runs to completion with no NaN.

explanation: Controller-driven body 1 goes NaN at final step. With controller enabled, body 1 position/velocity become non-finite while other bodies remain finite (pinned to floor). Disabling controller with identical initial conditions eliminates the NaN and energy stays bounded. Likely controller force/waypoint logic causes division by zero or numerical blow-up when body reaches target or collides with other bodies, corrupting state to NaN.
vision_note: Steps 2419-2421 show two blue bodies at the bottom left and a red body just above them with stable green waypoints. At step 2422 the red body vanishes, the right blue body jumps rightward and a green cross appears low near the floor, then the following tiles are solid black with no bodies rendered. [disagreement: The explanation claims the controller-driven body (orange) is the one that goes NaN, but the strip labels orange as controller and red as the violating body, and visibly it is the red non-controller body that disappears at the first violating step 2422, contradicting the claim that the controller body is the NaN source.]
